Method of Attack: Exploits over 80 known security flaws in software to infiltrate devices and co-opt them into a botnet for conducting DDoS attacks
Uses ChaCha20 algorithm to encrypt communications with the C2 server
Employs OpenNIC domain for C2 to evade detection
Shares the same key/nonce pair for the ChaCha20 algorithm as other botnets (hailBot, VapeBot, Woodman)
Impacted Systems: Devices from vendors such as Apache (ActiveMQ, Hadoop, Log4j, RocketMQ), Cacti, Cisco, D-Link, DrayTek, FreePBX, GitLab, Gocloud, Huawei, Jenkins, Linksys, Metabase, NETGEAR, Realtek, Seagate, SonicWall, Tenda, TOTOLINK, TP-Link, ZTE, Zyxel
Attack Vector: Exploitation of known vulnerabilities in software

Method of Attack: Variants of CatDDoS with little variation in code, communication design, strings, and decryption methods
Pulsing denial-of-service (PDoS) attack technique exploiting DNS queries and responses
Capitalizes on legitimate DNS features such as query rate limits, query-response timeouts, query aggregation, and maximum response size settings
Uses IP-spoofing to send multiple DNS queries to a domain controlled by the attacker, withholding responses to aggregate multiple replies
Creates timed floods of responses to overwhelm target systems
